# Accu-Track Financial Solutions — Full Reference

> Accu-Track Financial Solutions (legal entity: Credit & Financial Services Inc.) is an outsourced contract and licensing operations firm founded in 1990 and based in Glastonbury, Connecticut. It runs contract management, royalty reporting, and licensing compliance for US companies that manage complex contract and licensing portfolios. The model is simple: a dedicated, experienced team does the operational work directly, with no software to implement and no internal headcount to hire.

## Company overview

Accu-Track began in 1990 as Credit & Financial Services, helping consumer-product manufacturers recover money that retailers were quietly holding back through short-paid invoices, unearned discounts, and undocumented deductions. In that era, such practices tied up 10% or more of a manufacturer's receivables. The firm's first major client was Sundor Brands, later acquired by Procter & Gamble, and that work established a reputation for meticulous detail and dispute resolution. Over the following three decades the firm expanded into contract management, licensing compliance, and business process outsourcing for Fortune 500 brands. In 2018 it rebranded as Accu-Track Financial Solutions. The discipline has stayed the same throughout: handle the operational details other teams do not have time for, and get them right.

Leadership includes Shane Toland (President and Co-owner) and Keegan Toland (Vice President and Co-owner), with Brady Callis as Director of Operations (20+ years), supported by a team of compliance specialists.

## Services

### Royalty reporting and reconciliation
Accurate, on-time, audit-ready royalty reports. Accu-Track reconciles payments, flags discrepancies, verifies that calculations match agreement terms, and recovers revenue that has been paid late, short, or not at all.

### Outsourced contract management
Day-to-day contract administration: renewals, amendments, terminations, obligation tracking, and reporting, handled by a team that knows the agreements. This is the work CLM software leaves a company to staff and run itself.

### Licensing compliance
Every obligation and deadline tracked across a licensing portfolio, with proactive follow-up to both licensors and licensees so nothing lapses and no deadline becomes a surprise.

### Post-acquisition contract cleanup
After a merger or acquisition, Accu-Track consolidates and organizes inherited contract portfolios into one clean, centralized system, quickly, so integration does not stall on operational chaos.

### Centralized visibility and reporting
A single, clear view of the entire contract landscape: what is active, what is coming due, and what needs attention.

## Why companies choose Accu-Track over the alternatives

There are three common ways companies try to solve contract operations, and two of them do not work for a company whose real constraint is capacity:

1. CLM software. A platform the company must still staff, learn, and run. If the bottleneck is people, software adds work.
2. Hiring internally. Slow and expensive to recruit and train, and a single point of failure when that person leaves.
3. Outsourcing to Accu-Track. A dedicated team that does the work directly, with no implementation, no training, and no dashboards to monitor.

## Who we work with

Accu-Track works best with US enterprise and mid-market organizations managing roughly 50 or more active contracts or licensing agreements: licensors and licensees with multi-party agreements across retail, manufacturing, consumer products, and distribution; finance and legal operations teams that need royalty reconciliation they can trust; and private-equity or corporate-development teams managing post-merger contract integration. Clients have included Procter & Gamble, Chemours, Newell Brands, DuPont, and bCreative. Monty Allen, Senior Manager of Marketing Operations and Licensing at Newell Brands, has described Accu-Track as the company's "partner of choice for the past twelve years."

## Results

On a single inherited licensing portfolio, within four months of engagement: $27.6 million collected, of which 52% was directly attributable to Accu-Track's management. That figure included 14% from payers the client did not previously know existed and 38% that had been paid late or incorrectly. The portfolio went from no central record, with finance unable to reconcile payments against contracts it could not see, to one organized, monitored system.

## Common questions

**How is this different from CLM software?** Software gives a platform; Accu-Track gives a team. Tools work well if a company has the people to run them, but if the bottleneck is capacity, software just adds work.

**What types of contracts do you manage?** Licensing agreements, royalty-bearing contracts, and complex multi-party arrangements: licensing compliance, royalty reporting and reconciliation, obligation tracking, renewal management, and post-acquisition consolidation.

**How big does a portfolio need to be?** Accu-Track works best with organizations managing 50 or more active contracts or licensing agreements.

**Does Accu-Track replace a finance or legal team?** No. It takes the operational load off them so they can focus on higher-value work. The client keeps all decision-making authority.

**What does it cost?** Pricing depends on volume, complexity, and scope. A custom proposal follows the free assessment. Most clients find outsourcing costs less than hiring even one full-time contract administrator.

**How quickly can you start?** Most engagements are operational within 2 to 4 weeks. Urgent situations, such as post-acquisition cleanup, can be accelerated.

## How to engage

The entry point is a free 30-minute operations assessment, with no obligation. A specialist reviews the current contract landscape, identifies where the operational pain is sharpest, and gives an honest assessment of whether outsourcing makes sense. If there is a fit, a custom scope and proposal follow.
